chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you advance with your opponent to a governor or to a judge, stand to his right, meaning to the right of the opponent."

key_terms.خَصْمٍ: opponent / adversary in a legal dispute

ai.seo_question: Where should a litigant stand when appearing before a judge in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the procedural etiquette for litigants, instructing the plaintiff to stand to the right of the defendant when appearing before a judge or governor. This positioning reflects the traditional judicial hierarchy where the one presenting the claim occupies the position of honor relative to the respondent, ensuring clarity and respect in legal proceedings. It underscores the Shia emphasis on proper conduct (*adab*) not just in worship, but in civic and legal interactions as well.
